text:
The network has shifted from a contest over capacity to a contest over slots — and that is the single most important thing going on. Every one of the three monitored lanes is degraded at the same time, and the dominant instrument is now denial of berth access (closures, surcharges, allocation reviews) rather than new capacity. Assess with high confidence on the observed pattern; moderate confidence on the causal reading that this is a coherent shift rather than coincident disruptions. The arc: what actually changed. Reading back to June, the pivot is the Eastmere berth closure. Dredging closed the northern berth [R1]; a short reopening lifted calls briefly [R2], but it did not hold. By mid-September Northvale Freight was still diverting services [R3], and the Harbour Authority said reopening would follow the dredging schedule [R4]. That became the template. Since then: Halden Quay restricted its second terminal, leaving one berth in use [R5]. Feeder operators keep skipping the Westmark anchorage [R6]. Judgment (confidence ~0.75): the closure showed carriers that a single berth decision can cut regional throughput at low cost. That demonstration effect is the organising dynamic of the period. Throughput: wide, shallow, and stuck. Port; State; Evidence. Eastmere; Low calls; one berth closed [R1]; [R2] Halden Quay; One terminal restricted [R5]; [R6] The regulator's review is likely to keep allocation uncertain through the quarter. Not established: the exact sequence of events in the last 48 hours.

Stated confidence: 0.65
